restrictions: The two messages have 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 bytes for one t with 1 <= t < 2^32: t zero chunks of 1024 bytes followed by a last chunk of one block. The last chunk is compressed as a non-root chunk with counter t (v12 = t, v13 = 0), flags 3 and its true block length; the 63-byte block ends in eight zero bytes, so words 14 and 15 and the top byte of word 13 are zero in both zero-filled blocks. Equal last-chunk chaining values give equal digests by the tree lemma of proof.md Section 7.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.

Exact part: for every trial of proof.md Section 8 the two last-chunk chaining values agree on words 0, 2, 5 and 7, E1.c1 lies in the cube of beta* = 18b0e098, Y4 is held in the sub-class of 131,072 values, and the counter t is solved per trial as ROL(K0.d1,16) XOR K0.a1; trials with t = 0 are dropped. A frame (six outer words, the member y and its own D2.a1 = g*, all from one fresh 256-bit word) is one outer step. A 32-bit word K(D2.a1), computed by 29 assignments, equals an explicit word H(E1.d1, E1.a2) in every trial (Lemma AK, GPT Sol). Each frame computes K* = K(g*) alone and scans a fixed table of 53 * 2^26 E1 records; a kept record with H = K* is a root, so the search forms exactly the E1-listed trials of the outer step, at most 2^21, and certifies exactly its listed good trials (Lemmas KT, TG, TG1), at most 3,072 (Lemma S7). Heuristic part: over 2,487,937,099,176,099,696,050,654 frames, 2^102.042 trials, a collision is found with probability >= 0.39 under H1'.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5, 430 machine units (operations, loads, stores) per unit, 16 registers; every load is one unit wherever its word lies. Allowances in words from GPT Sol's answer AK, not counted by a program: per frame 4,096 for the random word and the 35 frame lines, 512 for the word K* (one value of D2.a1; no table of a frame is built), 64 per E1 record scanned (53 * 2^26 records), 8,192 per root (at most 2^21 per frame) for its reconstruction, the tests of Q*, t and rule A and two last-chunk compressions; 2^46 once for the E1 record table. The run halts with failure after 2,487,937,099,176,099,696,050,654 frames; every row is charged at its worst case. With the selection procedure in full, O_tot = 609,079,694,566,501,146,182,870,294,126,236,544 operations, T <= O_tot/430 + 2^38, log2 T = 110.12592 (proof.md Sections 9, 11).

Randomized by one fresh uniform 256-bit word per frame. The success probability 0.39 (bound 0.390002) holds only under H1', the rate at 5/7 of the model's conditional count, a margin of 1.40 where earlier entries on this track used half; it is not measured. No dependence premise is made: Lemma S7 proves at most 3,072 successes per outer step, and Lemma S8 then gives Pr(N_o > 0) >= E[N_o]/3,072 per frame; no premise on a group of outer steps is made. The organizer-run experiments run the root instance of the same construction (counter 0, flags 11), because no digest experiment can show a half-collision of a non-root chunk's chaining value. No full 2-round collision is exhibited and none was computed. The search of proof.md Section 9 is defined in the text only and has not been implemented; the submitted program contains steps CO and CT, the compression and the rule A test that it uses.

Six 32-bit constants, the word eta, two bits of the sub-class, three 32-bit constants of the rule test, the beta* cube and the seven tau values with eps are a fixed record of nonuniform advice stated in proof.md Section 12 (92 bytes); the success analysis uses only properties of it that the proof verifies exactly. The searches and counts that selected it are written as a selection procedure SEL with a stated range for every search and a stated cap on every run: preprocessing_log2 70 bounds SEL (498,959,035,065,866,484,184,960 operations: steps 1 to 3 at their cap S_old, steps 3a to 6 selecting the sub-class, rule A and beta*) and the E1 record table, both included in time_log2; SEL is not a premise. memory_log2_bytes 44 covers the two output messages (each below 2^42 bytes), the code, SEL and the search (below 2^37 bytes: the E1 record table, 113,816,633,344 bytes), all held at once. No priority or novelty claim is made.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. For an outer step of the counter construction whose seven outer words are independent uniform 32-bit words and whose member y is uniform in the sub-class of 131,072 values, let N_o be the number of its listed good valid trials over all of the cube Q* of beta* = 18b0e098: t != 0, equal last-chunk chaining values (R = 0), rule A, and an E1 outcome among the seven outcomes of beta*. Assume E[N_o] >= (2^21 - 1) q with q = (5/7) p = 5 * 1033 / (7 * 2^101), about 2^-91.473, where p = 1033 * 2^-101 is the conditional model rate of Lemma S1. Nothing is assumed about the dependence of the good trials: Lemma S7 proves N_o <= 3,072 in every outer step with no law of the outer words, so E[N_o (N_o - 1)] <= 3,071 E[N_o] for every law, and Lemma S8 with b(3,071) = 1/3,072 gives Pr(N_o > 0) >= E[N_o] / 3,072. Each frame of the search of proof.md 9.1 is one such outer step, drawn from its own fresh 256-bit word, so the frames are independent; the run's 2,487,937,099,176,099,696,050,654 frames give FRAMES * E[N_o] / 3,072 >= 0.4943, and the probability that no frame has N_o > 0 is at most exp(-0.4943) < 0.609998. The premise is a first-moment statement: it asserts neither independent trials nor independent uniform E1 or E3 words. It is the rate part of the premise of entry e7b17fd1 and its successors on this track, with the count restricted to the seven outcomes and the factor at 5/7 of the count in place of one half; their factorial part is not assumed.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Sections 8 and 9: lengths 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 with a non-root last chunk (counter t < 2^32, v13 = 0, flags 3), the six constants of Section 3.2, Y4 in the sub-class of 131,072 values, E1.c1 in Q*, t solved per trial and t = 0 dropped, the seven outer words and the member drawn from one fresh 256-bit word per frame. N_o counts all of Q* in the frame's one outer step; the search certifies exactly these trials (Lemma TG1). Nothing is assumed about a group of more than one outer step.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the participant's exact count, in integer arithmetic under the seven-word model, of the beta* part of the sub-class kept by rule A (seven outcomes, 67,698,688 = 1033 * 2^16; the counting program and its output are printed in Section 17), times 2^11 for drawing E1.c1 from the cube (Lemma S1: conditioning the model on the cube leaves the E3 side unchanged), taken at 5/7, a margin of 1.40 chosen by the participant; entry e7b17fd1 and the earlier entries on this track took half. The dependence of the good trials of one outer step is not extrapolated: the success bound uses only the proved worst case N_o <= 3,072 (Lemma S7). Participant evidence of Section 13, untrusted by the harness: 2^45.6 real 32-bit counter trials whose measurable partial events match the exact model within about 1% to about 2^-31.7, and a reduced-width (8-bit) end-to-end run of complete messages in which the counter arrangement found 251 collisions against 255.0 predicted. The joint 128-bit event itself, about 2^-91 per trial, is not measured at 32 bits.
heuristics.limitations: The factor (5/7) * 138,646,913,024 = 99,033,509,302.86 per 2^128 is assumed; at 5/7 the premise is stronger than the half-count premise of the earlier entries and is not implied by it. The dependence bound used is the proved worst case of Lemma S7, so single outer steps that differ strongly in partial events (a variance 572 times the mean for rule A) do not weaken the success bound; the worst case costs a factor 3,072 in frames, 11.585 in the exponent. The organizer-run experiments run the root instance (counter 0, flags 11) and measure neither the factor nor the counter half-collision. The transfer of the single-trial law to the construction is partly proved (Lemmas S1 to S4 and IP) and partly assumed here; the share of the success mass carried by the dropped member with t = 0 is not bounded. No measurement of this premise exists at its scale, and the search has not been implemented.
